_meta.purpose: Publishable rule-change events for the public changes feed.
_meta.separable: Deliberately independent of the mobility determination engine, which is HELD from production. The feed publishes change facts + citations only.
_meta.status_derivation: Structured fields ONLY (rule_changes_on presence + direction). Status is NOT inferred from prose: 27 of 55 records match enacted/proposed/rule signals simultaneously, so a regex label would be a guess. Records whose status cannot be established from structure are not emitted.
_meta.reverification_rule: needs_reverification=true means the effective date has passed and we have NOT re-checked. The page must say 'effective [date]; we re-verify on/after that date' -- never 'is now in effect'.

events.citation: 32 M.R.S. § 12232 (individual practice privilege); 32 M.R.S. § 12252(1), (8) (firm license triggers; peer review); 32 M.R.S. § 12253 (out-of-state firm practice privilege); 02-280 C.M.R. ch. 6 (Accounting Firm License Requirements)
events.detail: FLUX IS A SOURCE DISAGREEMENT, NOT A PENDING LAW CHANGE. (1) Board web guidance vs. statute on FIRM registration: 32 M.R.S. § 12252(1)(A)(3), as amended by PL 2021, c. 68, § 2, requires a firm license for an out-of-state firm performing § 12201(3-A)(A),(C),(D) attest work for a Maine home-office client 'unless: (a) It qualifies for a firm license pursuant to subsections 3 and 8 and it performs such services through an individual with practice privileges under section 12232; or (b) It meets the requirements of section 12253.' The Board's OWN pages (Licensing - Accountancy Firm and Accountancy Branch, and the firm FAQ answering the question 'Substantial Equivalency?') still publish the PRE-2021 unqualified trigger with the 'unless' carve-outs omitted entirely and with no mention of § 12253. That is stale board guidance reading MORE restrictively than current law. The codified BOARD RULE (02-280 ch. 6 § 1(A)) does NOT conflict: it incorporates the statute by reference ('when licensure is required by 32 M.R.S. §12252(1)(A)'), so statute and compiled rule agree; only the informational board webpage is out of date. Recorded firm_registration_attest=false per the statute + compiled rule, but a firm relying on the exemption should confirm with the Board, whose published guidance would tell it to register. (2) rule_changes_on = 2021-10-18 is the operative changeover on which the current firm-mobility scheme took effect: PL 2021, c. 68 ('An Act To Enable Out-of-state Certified Public Accountancy Firms To Provide Services in Maine on the Basis of Substantial Equivalency', H.P. 124 / L.D. 171), approved by the Governor May 25, 2021, contains NO emergency preamble and NO separate effective-date section (confirmed against the enrolled act PDF 130LR0636(03)), so it took effect 90 days after the 130th Legislature's First Special Session adjourned sine die on July 19, 2021, i.e. October 18, 2021 (Me. Const. art. IV, pt. 3, § 16; corroborated by the Revisor's note at 18-B M.R.S. § 1229 that PL 2021, c. 235 'takes effect October 1, 2021' but the actual effective date was October 18, 2021, 90 days after adjournment of the First Special Session of the 130th Legislature). (3) NO 2025-26 mobility change in Maine — Maine is an outlier in the national wave. I scanned all 2,153 LD titles of the 132nd Legislature (2025-2026, LD 1 through LD 2245, adjourned sine die): exactly ONE accountancy bill exists, LD 1789 / H.P. 1200 'An Act to Amend the Education Requirements in the Certified Public Accountant Licensure Laws', enacted and signed June 12, 2025 as PL 2025, c. 297, which amends ONLY 32 M.R.S. § 12228(3) (120-hour exam-sitting eligibility). Its pathways/mobility provisions were stripped by Committee Amendment C-A (H-533) before passage. Sections 12232, 12252 and 12253 were untouched by the 2025 and 2026 sessions. No board rulemaking on mobility either: the 02-280 2025-2026 Regulatory Agenda lists only conformance reviews plus expected rulemaking 'to implement legislation governing licensure by endorsement and provisional licensure' (10 M.R.S. § 8003-H) — that is LICENSURE by endorsement, not practice privilege. A future mobility bill in the 133rd Legislature (convenes Dec 2026) is plausible given the stripped 2025 attempt, but nothing is pending now.

events.citation: RCW 18.04.350 (individual practice privileges); RCW 18.04.195(1) (firm license and firm-mobility exemptions); WAC 4-30-090 (practice privileges, as amended by WSR 25-10-028 eff. 2025-05-30)
events.detail: Washington completed its 2025-wave mobility rewrite by BOARD RULE, not statute: WSR 25-10-028 (filed 2025-04-29, effective 2025-05-30) rewrote WAC 4-30-090 from a substantial-equivalency test to individual criteria (current good-standing license from any US jurisdiction + at time of licensure bachelor's degree, passed Uniform CPA Exam, and one year of experience). A second rulemaking, WSR 25-21-108 (effective 2025-11-20), added three licensure pathways (incl. bachelor's + 2 yrs experience) and, per the board's rulemaking page, 'guardrails for the updated practice privilege rule'. The statute, RCW 18.04.350 (last amended 2024 c 13 / HB 1920, effective 2024-06-06 per the legislature's bill page), still frames mobility as a substantial-equivalency presumption with a state-level prong (1)(a) and individual prong (1)(b); the board page likewise still says 'qualifications are substantially equivalent' without stating the new WAC criteria. This is a framing mismatch, not an operative contradiction: WAC 4-30-010 defines substantial equivalency as 'a determination by the board or its designee', and WAC 4-30-090 is that determination. No pending 2025-26 accountancy bill found (2026 HB 1920 is unrelated). Watch for a statute-conformity bill and any further WAC 4-30-090 rulemaking.

events.citation: S.C. Code Ann. § 40-2-245 (individual practice privilege); § 40-2-30(I) (out-of-state firm no-registration privilege); § 40-2-40(B)(3) (firm registration trigger); § 40-2-255(C) (peer review); as amended by 2025 Act No. 34 (S.176), eff. June 30, 2025
events.detail: SC's 2025-wave rewrite is COMPLETE, not pending: 2025 Act No. 34 (S.176, signed May 12, 2025) took effect June 30, 2025 (flat effective clause 'This act takes effect on June 30, 2025'; passage was unanimous — Senate 41-0, House 111-0 — so no supermajority/immediate-effect question arises). It replaced the prior substantial-equivalency framework with a license-based test: § 40-2-245(A) now requires only (1) passed Uniform CPA Exam, (2) active certificate/license/permit from any state/territory/DC or IQAB-MRA foreign authority, and (3) legal authorization in the issuing jurisdiction. Firm mobility (§ 40-2-30(I)) dates to 2022 Act No. 174 and was retained/realigned by Act 34. No pending 2026 SC legislation touching Ch. 40-2 mobility was found. Board guidance is consistent with the statute, though the out-of-state firm form is dated 6/23 (pre-Act 34) — see notes. UPDATE (verifier - this field was REFUTED as false and is now TRUE): Board of Accountancy Regulation Document No. 5420 is actively pending - Notice of Drafting 2025-06-27, proposed in State Register Vol. 49 Issue 10 (2025-10-24), amending Reg 1-01 (licensure) and Reg 1-05 (firm registration, NEW sections (D)-(E)) to conform to Act 34, awaiting General Assembly approval via S.1167 (in Senate LCI committee since 2026-05-06). The statutory individual-mobility rule (no notice/fee) is NOT amended by it, but the pending Reg 1-05 firm-registration sections sit directly under this record's firm fields. The researcher's sentence "No pending 2026 SC legislation touching Ch. 40-2 mobility was found" is superseded by this finding.

events.citation: Tenn. Code Ann. § 62-1-117 (Mobility), as rewritten by 2025 Tenn. Pub. Ch. 524 (SB 1316/HB 1330, 'Less is More Act of 2025'), § 38, eff. 2025-07-01; firm permits: Tenn. Code Ann. §§ 62-1-108, 62-1-113; peer review: Tenn. Code Ann. § 62-1-201(b); Tenn. Comp. R. & Regs. 0020-01-.11, 0020-01-.13, 0020-06-.04
events.detail: Statutory changeover already occurred: Pub. Ch. 524 § 38 (rewriting § 62-1-117 to automatic individual mobility with no notice/fee) took effect 2025-07-01 per § 65(c) of the act ('SECTIONS 1-31, 33, 34, and 36-64 of this act take effect on July 1, 2025'); the new licensure-pathway sections (§§ 32, 35: 150hr+1yr or 120hr+2yr) took effect 2026-01-01 per § 65(b). No supermajority-conditioned immediate-effect clause is involved; the act states its own dates (House 60-31, Senate 24-6 recorded for reference). Residual flux: board rules Chapters 0020-01 through 0020-05 predate the act (0020-01 last revised May 2024) and the board voted in 2026 to open rulemaking to conform them to the Less is More Act plus a retrospective review; Chapter 0020-06 (peer review) was already amended effective 2025-09-28. Rule 0020-01-.13 (Interstate Practice) simply defers to § 62-1-117 for out-of-state individuals, so no statute-vs-rule contradiction exists on mobility. No pending 2026-session accountancy mobility bills found on the General Assembly subject index.

events.citation: Tex. Occ. Code §§ 901.461, 901.462 (practice privileges); § 901.351(a-1) (firm license required only if office in Texas); as amended by Acts 2025, 89th Leg., R.S., Ch. 40 (S.B. 522), § 2, eff. Sept. 1, 2025; 22 TAC § 517.2 (as amended eff. 2025-10-09)
events.detail: SB 522 (89th Leg., 2025, Ch. 40) rewrote the individual mobility test effective 2025-09-01: it deleted the NASBA NQAS substantial-equivalency test from 901.462(a) and replaced it with individual criteria (passed uniform CPA exam + education pathway of (A) 150-hr baccalaureate w/ accounting concentration, (B) graduate degree w/ accounting concentration, or (C) baccalaureate w/ accounting concentration + experience of 1 year for pathways A/B or 2 years for pathway C, measured at time of home-state licensure). The enrolled SB 522 text and the compiled statute AGREE exactly - no enrolled-vs-compiled contradiction. However, the TSBPA's own practice-privilege page (fetched 2026-07-31) STILL describes the repealed pre-SB 522 NASBA NQAS substantial-equivalency checklist - board page and statute currently DISAGREE on the equivalence test; the board page appears stale, not evidence of a pending change. 901.462(f) grandfathers individuals who on 2024-12-31 held an out-of-state license and practiced under the privilege. Firm-side rules (901.461 full firm mobility) unchanged since HB 1520 eff. 2019-09-01. UPDATE (verifier): the board HAS conformed its rules - 22 TAC 517.2 was amended to delete the NASBA NQAS reference and add no notice/fee/registration requirement (proposed 50 TexReg 4198, 2025-07-25; adopted without changes; filed with SOS 2025-09-19; effective 2025-10-09), and 22 TAC 501.53 (eff. 2025-04-02) requires privilege practitioners to comply with all Board rules of professional conduct. The legal test is therefore settled at BOTH statute and rule level; the only remaining disagreement is the stale TSBPA web page, so rule_in_flux=true is a conservative flag AssetLab may judge narrowable once the board page updates. Adjacent 2025 enactments (do not change any field): SB 262 adds a home-state licensure pathway operative 2026-08-01 (120-hr bachelor's + 2 yrs experience; TSBPA rules eff. 2025-10-10), which affects how pathway-C comparability under 901.462(a) is exercised by inbound CPAs; SB 522 § 1 also amended 901.259 (reciprocal certification, incl. NQAS verification route).

events.citation: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 20-281n (repealed and replaced by P.A. 25-36, § 4, eff. Oct. 1, 2025); Conn. Gen. Stat. §§ 20-281e(g)-(i), 20-281(b)
events.detail: P.A. 25-36 (HB 7020, approved 2025-06-10, each section expressly 'Effective October 1, 2025' -- explicit date in act text, no supermajority-contingent immediate-effect clause) repealed the NASBA-NQAS substantial-equivalency test in Sec. 20-281n and the statutory definitions of 'NASBA' and 'substantial equivalency', replacing them with an individual-criteria test (out-of-state license in good standing + meets CT education/experience/exam requirements of new Sec. 20-281c(b)-(e)) plus a grandfather clause (exam passed on or before 2025-09-30 and licensed in good standing on 2025-09-30 = privilege without meeting new criteria). Changeover is PAST and operative. Residual flux: (1) the CGA 'current' compiled chapter (cga.ct.gov/current/pub/chap_389.htm) still displays the PRE-act 20-281n text (history ends at P.A. 15-181) with only a header note deferring to a '2026 Supplement, revised to January 1, 2026' that is not posted at any fetchable /current/sup/ URL -- rely on the official act text, not the compiled page; (2) CT Society of CPAs (lead only) reports the Board of Accountancy is still working through implementing regulations and a comprehensive statute/regulation modernization review; the admin regs (Regs. Conn. State Agencies 20-280-1 et seq.) could not be verified as updated post-P.A. 25-36; (3) DCP firm-permit guidance says a permit is triggered by 'any attest or compilation services to Connecticut clients' while statute 20-281e(h) exempts no-office firms' SSARS reviews/compilations if quality-review-qualified and working through a privilege holder -- for compilation-only engagements record the conservative (permit) reading; attest itself is consistent across both. No 2026-session (adjourned 2026-05-06) amendment to ch. 389 mobility sections found; P.A. 25-111 (SB 1357, DCP omnibus) does not touch Secs. 20-279b to 20-281n.

events.citation: Md. Code Ann., Bus. Occ. & Prof. § 2-321 (individual practice privilege, as amended by Ch. 406 of 2025 / SB 51, eff. 2025-10-01); § 2-401 (firm permit + no-office firm exemptions); § 2-4A-02 (peer review)
events.detail: Three items. (1) 2025 SB 51 / Ch. 406 rewrote the §2-321 equivalency test effective 2025-10-01 (already operative): out-of-state CPA is deemed substantially equivalent if the individual holds a valid CPA license from another state AND was required to pass the Uniform CPA Examination for it — decoupling MD mobility from other states' 150-hour changes. Effective-date clause is the standard 'October 1, 2025' (verified on official mgaleg bill page; not an emergency/supermajority-conditional clause; passed 45-0 Senate, 140-0 House). (2) 2026 HB 643 / Ch. 174 (new bachelor's+2yr licensure pathway) is enacted but NOT effective until 2026-10-01; it amends only §§2-302 and 2-303 (licensure qualifications) and does NOT touch §2-321 mobility or §2-401 firm rules. (3) SOURCE DISAGREEMENT: the Board's firm-permit application page (cpaapplyfirm.shtml) still states out-of-state firms 'must obtain a permit' ('This requirement also pertains to CPA firms that are located in other states'), contradicting §2-401 (firm-mobility exemption effective 2019-10-01) and the Board's own firm-mobility page ('CPA firms that are licensed in another state will not have to hold a firm permit in Maryland'). The apply page appears stale (pre-2019); statute + the Board's dedicated mobility pages agree, so firm_registration_attest is recorded false, but the conflict is flagged here per protocol.

events.citation: AS 08.04.420 (practice privileges); AS 08.04.422 (conditions of practice privileges); AS 08.04.240 (firm permit — subsection (k), the former out-of-state attest-firm permit, repealed by sec. 22, ch. 22, SLA 2025); AS 08.04.565 (attest through a firm); AS 08.04.426 (peer review); 12 AAC 04.245; 12 AAC 04.251; 12 AAC 04.285; 12 AAC 04.600. Amending act: HB 121, ch. 22, SLA 2025 (34th Leg.), eff. Jan. 1, 2026.
events.detail: Two things put Alaska in flux. (1) COMPLETED 2025-26 CHANGEOVER: HB 121 (34th Leg.) became law without the governor's signature on 2025-07-23 as CHAPTER 22 SLA 25. Enrolled sec. 24: 'Except as provided in sec. 23 of this Act, this Act takes effect January 1, 2026.' Sec. 23 gave immediate effect under AS 01.10.070(c) only to secs. 14-21 (the private-professional-conservator/probate provisions); ALL accounting provisions (secs. 1-13 and 22) are governed by the fixed Jan. 1, 2026 date, so no supermajority-conditioned immediate-effect analysis applies to them. (Final passage was in any event unanimous and far above two-thirds of members elected: House PASSED Y38 E2 and concurred in the Senate amendment Y40 of 40 elected; Senate PASSED Y20 N- of 20 elected; the legislature's bill history records '(H) EFFECTIVE DATE(S) OF LAW SEE CHAPTER'.) HB 121 sec. 4 struck the entire substantial-equivalency test out of AS 08.04.420(a) (the [BRACKETED CAPITALS] 150-hour / exam / 1-year-experience / individually-substantially-equivalent conditions are deleted language), sec. 5 extended the no-notice/no-fee clause of AS 08.04.420(c) from individuals to firms, sec. 6 added firm mobility at AS 08.04.420(d)-(e), sec. 13 amended AS 08.04.565 to let attest be performed through a firm operating under a practice privilege, and sec. 22 repealed AS 08.04.240(k) (the former out-of-state attest-firm permit). (2) LIVE PRIMARY-SOURCE DISAGREEMENT on firm_registration_attest: the compiled, still-in-force administrative rule 12 AAC 04.245(a)(2) (official Alaska Administrative Code at akleg.gov, and reprinted unchanged in the board's own Rev. 1/01/2026 'Statutes and Regulations Public Accountancy') states that a firm 'must obtain a permit issued by the board under this chapter if the firm ... (2) does not have an established and maintained office in the state but provides, or offers to provide, attest functions in the state under AS 08.04.240(k)'. Its operative statutory hook, AS 08.04.240(k), was REPEALED effective 2026-01-01, and AS 08.04.420(d) + AS 08.04.565(2) now authorize attest through an out-of-state no-office firm under a practice privilege. The board's last accountancy rulemaking was adopted 2025-06-05, filed 2025-06-26 and effective 2025-07-26 (Register 255, Oct. 2025) — it predates HB 121's effective date and did not touch 12 AAC 04.245, so the rule has not been conformed. Statute and compiled rule therefore state OPPOSITE answers for firm_registration_attest; per the conservative rule this record carries TRUE, not the permissive value. Note that the board's own current guidance sides with the statute (see notes), so the practical answer is very likely 'no permit required' — but that is not what the codified rule says today.

events.citation: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code §§ 5096-5096.22 (Accountancy Act, Art. 5.1 Practice Privileges), as amended by AB 1175 (Stats. 2025, ch. 293), eff. 2026-01-01; esp. §§ 5096(a)-(b) (individual open mobility, no notice/fee), 5096(c) (attest via registered firm), 5096(h) (7-year discipline pre-notification), 5096.12 (out-of-state firm registration)
events.detail: AB 1175 (Stats. 2025, ch. 293, signed 2025-10-03, eff. 2026-01-01) replaced California's substantial-equivalency practice privilege with an 'open mobility' framework: any current-and-active out-of-state license qualifies, no notice/fee, and no equivalency test; the CBA may withdraw a specific state's no-notice privilege (BPC 5096.21/5096.22), in which case that state's licensees must file a notification form and pay fees. HOWEVER, the CBA's own Licensee FAQs (last updated 2026-05-04, AFTER the effective date) and practice-privilege pages STILL describe the pre-2026 regime (license from a substantially equivalent state, 4-of-last-10-years practice, or individually equivalent qualifications) - board guidance and the compiled statute currently disagree; practitioner-facing confusion risk is high until CBA guidance conforms. UPDATE (verifier): the CBA has ACTIVE AB 1175 implementation rulemaking (initiated Nov 2025; 16 CCR amendments incl. sections 5.5 and 19 approved Sept 2025 and reauthorized with corrections; 'accounting concentration' definition on the July 2026 board agenda). Separately, AB 1175's licensure-pathway changes phase in 2027-01-01 (new B&P 5093.2/5093.3 pathway) through 2029-01-01 (150-hr legacy route sunset) - licensure, not mobility, but it will change the inbound-CPA population profile. Monitor for CBA guidance/regulation updates and any state-specific privilege withdrawals under 5096.21.

events.citation: O.C.G.A. 43-3-18(b) (individual mobility practice privileges), 43-3-16(b) (firm licensure), 43-3-17 (peer review), as amended by 2025 Ga. Laws Act 87 (HB 148), eff. 2026-01-01; Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 20-3-.09, 20-8-.01, 20-8-.02
events.detail: HB 148 (Act 87, signed 2025-05-09) rewrote Georgia mobility effective 2026-01-01: term 'substantial equivalency' replaced with 'mobility practice privileges' and the old NASBA-style state-level test (license from a state requiring 150 hrs + exam + 1 yr experience, with individual-equivalence fallback) was replaced by individual criteria (current license in good standing + education/experience 'as the board by rule or regulation may establish' + passed Uniform CPA Exam). SOURCE DISAGREEMENT (stale board materials): the board's compiled rules -- 20-3-.09 (last amended eff. 2015-02-24), 20-8-.01 (2016), 20-8-.02 (2015), all 'current through Rules and Regulations filed through July 20, 2026' on rules.sos.ga.gov -- and the board's Statement of Policy No. 11 (adopted 2015-11-18, still posted on gsba.georgia.gov) still state the superseded regime, including the old condition that the individual hold a license 'in a state which grants similar practice privileges to license holders in this state.' The board published proposed conforming amendments (August 2025 rule synopses: 20-3-.02, 20-3-.05, 20-3-.08, 20-3-.09, 20-7-.01, 20-8-.01, 20-8-.02, each 'to go into effect January 1, 2026'), but the amended texts do NOT yet appear in the compiled GAC as of 2026-07-31 -- final adoption status unresolved. Until the board adopts education/experience criteria under new 43-3-18(b)(1)(A), the operative individual criteria are effectively good-standing license + passed exam. New 43-3-16(b)(1)(C) also added an 'unless such firm meets the requirements of paragraph (2)' escape and added compilations (43-3-2 para. (4)) to the licensure trigger; (b)(2) by its terms only authorizes review/other-examination-AUP/compilation services without a license, so the conservative reading (audit/SSAE-examination/PCAOB work still requires a firm license) is used here. UPDATE (verifier, markup-verified enrolled act): HB 148 ALSO enacted conditional FIRM mobility effective 2026-01-01 - in 43-3-16(b)(1)(C) the phrase 'subparagraph (A), (C), or (D) of' is STRICKEN and in (b)(2) 'subparagraphs (B) and (E) of' is stricken, so a no-office firm meeting 43-3-16(b)(2)(A)-(C) (majority-CPA ownership, peer-review compliance, performance through a Georgia-licensed or mobility-privileged individual) may perform ALL 43-3-2(2) attest services (audit, prospective-financial examination, PCAOB engagements) plus (4) compilations WITHOUT a Georgia firm license; old 43-3-16(b)(3) (no-office firms/other services under CPA title) is stricken in its entirety. HOWEVER the compiled board rules as served by rules.sos.ga.gov (current through rules filed 2026-07-20) DIRECTLY CONFLICT: Rule 20-8-.01(1) still flatly mandates biennial licensure for any no-office firm performing audit/SSAE-examination/PCAOB work directed into Georgia, with no (b)(2) exemption, and Rule 20-3-.09/20-8-.02 plus the GSBA 2015 Statement of Policy and FAQ pages still describe the superseded substantial-equivalency regime. Statute and still-compiled rule state OPPOSITE answers for the same firm - a live primary-source conflict, NOT resolved here per the contradiction rule: firm_registration_attest is kept at the CONSERVATIVE true (register) and rule_in_flux stays true until the board's conforming amendments land.

events.citation: NMSA 1978 §§ 61-28B-26, 61-28B-11(B), 61-28B-13, as amended by Laws 2025, ch. 105 (HB 296), eff. Jan. 1, 2026; implementing rules NMAC 16.60.3.14 and 16.60.4.8(F)
events.detail: NM joined the 2025-26 wave: HB 296 (Laws 2025, ch. 105, signed 2025-04-08, House 61-0 / Senate 39-1) rewrote the Public Accountancy Act effective 2026-01-01 (explicit Section 9 effective-date clause, no supermajority contingency) — replaced the old 150-hour substantial-equivalency privilege in 61-28B-26 with a two-prong comparable-licensure/exam-based test, added a broad exam-only no-notice privilege in 61-28B-11(B), and added no-permit firm mobility for attest in 61-28B-13(C). The statutory changeover is PAST (in force since 2026-01-01). Still mid-flight: board rulemaking — a 2025-12-09 rule hearing proposed amendments to all five NMAC 16.60 parts, but as of 2026-07-31 the compiled NMAC at srca.nm.gov still shows pre-HB296 versions (16.60.3.14 last amended 12/12/2021, still framed on the repealed 'substantial equivalency' test). The stale rule does NOT state an opposite answer on any recorded field (its no-notice/no-fee and no-permit-attest-firm provisions agree with the new statute). Board FAQ is also stale/incomplete: it states a firm permit is required only 'if the firm has an office in New Mexico,' omitting the statute's default that a no-office firm rendering attest for a NM client needs a permit UNLESS it meets the 61-28B-13(C) conditions.

P.L.2025, c.384 (A5598 2R, approved Jan 20, 2026; effective the 30th day next following enactment = 2026-02-19) rewrote N.J.S.A. 45:2B-50.1, replacing the NASBA/NQAS substantial-equivalency test with individual criteria (current valid unrevoked CPA license from any state + passed Uniform CPA Exam or board-approved exam + one year of experience per C.45:2B-51). The compiled admin rule N.J.A.C. 13:29-4.1 (readopted WITHOUT amendment eff. 2024-11-26, 57 N.J.R. 55(a), expires 2031) still states the old NASBA NQAS state-level/individual-verification test; no implementing rulemaking found as of 2026-07-31 -- statute controls but rule text disagrees on the equivalence test (both grant privilege with no notice/fee, so the boolean fields are unaffected). Date discrepancy: NJCPA/press report signing Jan 12, 2026 and effectiveness Feb 11, 2026, but the official chapter law prints 'P.L. 2025, CHAPTER 384, approved January 20, 2026' and the official legislative digest lists 1/20/2026 -> official effective date is 2026-02-19; recorded per official documents.

events.citation: Mont. Code Ann. § 37-50-325 (practice privilege for nonresident certified public accountant -- rules); § 37-50-335 (registration of firms -- exemptions); § 37-50-330 (firm ownership); ARM 24.201.531 (practice privilege); ARM 24.201.1108 (peer review alternatives and exemptions)
events.detail: Montana's MOBILITY provisions themselves were NOT amended in the 2025-26 wave: MCA 37-50-325 (individual practice privilege) and 37-50-335 (firm mobility) both carry history ending at 'amd. Sec. 3/5, Ch. 162, L. 2017' in the Montana Code Annotated 2025, and board rule ARM 24.201.531 (PRACTICE PRIVILEGE) is still the version effective 2014-11-21. Montana was nonetheless touched by the wave on adjacent fronts, all now already operative: (1) SB 166 (Ch. 346, L. 2025) rewrote the education pathway in MCA 37-50-305, dropping the express 150-semester-hour rule in favor of board-set coursework -- enrolled act Sec. 2 reads 'Effective date. [This act] is effective January 1, 2026' (delayed effective date stated in the act's own title; no immediate-effect/supermajority option, so no vote-count check was needed); implementing board rules ARM 24.201.502/.503/.516 were amended effective 2025-09-13 (MAR Notice 2025-167.2). Watch item, not a present conflict: Montana now has two coexisting equivalency mechanisms -- ARM 24.201.531(2) (NASBA-approved jurisdictions deemed substantially equivalent, governs PRACTICE PRIVILEGE) and ARM 24.201.527 (board-published list, governs ENDORSEMENT). Flux is nevertheless TRUE for two independent reasons. (1) SOURCE DISAGREEMENT ON THE EQUIVALENCE TEST: the still-compiled Board legislative rule, W. Va. C.S.R. §1-1-10.1 (1CSR1, filed and effective March 29, 2024, i.e. pre-H.B. 4088), provides that 'In determining whether the certification requirements of the other state or the individual are substantially equivalent to the certification requirements of the Uniform Accountancy Act, the Board is authorized to use the NQAS' -- a UAA-benchmarked test that expressly permits reliance on NASBA's National Qualification Appraisal Service and expressly permits a STATE-level ('the other state') determination. As a WV legislative rule it still requires legislative authorization (W. Va. Code ch. 64) before it can take effect, so the earliest operative date is the 2027 regular session. (3) STALE BOARD WEB GUIDANCE: the Board's Mobility page (Page Updated 9/4/2020) still describes mobility as running 'from a substantially equivalent state' (state-level framing), and the Board's CPA Licensure FAQ (Page Updated 9/24/2021) still recites the '150-hour academic specifications' and a flat one-year experience requirement, both superseded by H.B. 4088's three-pathway §30-9-8. events.detail: Idaho IS part of the 2025-26 wave and changed on 2026-07-01 -- 30 days before the verification date. H0563 (2026 Sess. Idaho Const. art. events.detail: STARTING HINT WAS WRONG on the chapter: South Dakota accountancy law is SDCL ch. 36-20B (not 36-36/36-36A); rules are ARSD art. 20:75. South Dakota IS part of the 2025-26 wave. 2026 HB 1035 (Rep. Weisgram et al.), enacted as SL 2026, ch 160, rewrote SDCL 36-20B-66 and 36-20B-67 and took effect 2026-07-01 -- i.e. 30 days before this verification date. EFFECTIVE-DATE CHECK PERFORMED: the enrolled text of HB 1035 (mylrc doc 303860) contains NO emergency clause and NO effective-date section (zero hits for 'emergency' and 'effective' in the enrolled text), so the SDCL 2-14-16 default applies: an act passed at a regular session that does not prescribe when it takes effect 'takes effect on the first day of July after its passage.' Signed by the Governor 2026-03-02. Final-passage votes were House 67-0 (of 70 elected) and Senate 34-0 (of 35 elected) -- a supermajority WAS present in both chambers, so an emergency clause would have carried, but none was included; therefore the fallback date 2026-07-01 governs, not immediate effect. The SD Legislature does not publish a per-bill 'effective date' line, so the date is derived from SDCL 2-14-16 plus the absence of an emergency clause. PRE-2026 LAW: the old 36-20B-66 was the 2009 UAA substantial-equivalency provision; HB 1035 replaced the equivalency framing with explicit individual education/experience criteria and added the express 'no notice, fee, or other submission' sentence. 36-20B-67 now grandfathers anyone who exercised privileges under the pre-2026 section on or before 2024-12-31. PARALLEL BOARD RULEMAKING: the Board held a rules hearing 2026-04-30; those rules were filed as 52 SDR 125 and also took effect 2026-07-01 (visible in the source line of ARSD 20:75:03:15, which was retitled from 'Substantial equivalency and reciprocity' to 'Issuance of certificate to applicant licensed by another state' and had 'substantially equivalent' struck in favor of 'comparable'). Those rules touched education/experience/reciprocity, NOT the mobility or firm-permit rules. NO PRIMARY-SOURCE DISAGREEMENT FOUND: the board's mobility page has been updated and reproduces the new 36-20B-66 text verbatim, and no ARSD rule contradicts the statute. One residual stale artifact: the board mobility page still opens with the legacy sentence 'South Dakota is a substantially equivalent state.' and links to CPAmobility.org, which is inconsistent in framing with the statute's move away from an equivalency test; it does not contradict any field value. Flagged in flux because the changeover is only 30 days old, secondary/NASBA guidance is likely to lag, and the Board's 2026-08-12 meeting agenda was not yet posted as of this verification.

events.citation: Utah Code 58-26a-305 (exemptions from licensure / practice privilege, as amended by S.B. 15, Laws of Utah 2025, ch. 283, eff. 2026-07-01); Utah Code 58-26a-301(1)(b) and 58-26a-302(3) (firm registration, as amended by S.B. 117, 2026 G.S. (compiled as ch. 64), eff. 2026-07-01); Utah Admin. Code R156-26a-305 and R156-26a-303a (as amended by Filing No. 58008, eff. 2026-07-08)
events.detail: Utah is mid-changeover in the 2025-26 wave. S.B. 15 (Laws of Utah 2025, ch. 283) took effect 2026-07-01 via a flat special-effective-date clause ('This bill takes effect on July 1, 2026' -- no supermajority condition, so no vote-count analysis needed; it passed unanimously regardless). It deleted the NASBA National Qualification Appraisal Service substantial-equivalency test from 58-26a-305 and replaced it with: valid out-of-state license in good standing + evidence at time of licensure of passing qualifying examinations; the pre-existing no-notice/no-fee clause carried forward. DOPL's implementing rule amendment (Filing No. 58008, published Utah State Bulletin 2026-06-01, effective 2026-07-08 per Bulletin 2026-07-15) conformed R156-26a to S.B. 15 and S.B. 117 (2026). LIVE CONFLICT on the firm fields: amended statute 58-26a-305(1)(a) exempts only 'an individual', and 58-26a-301(1)(b) requires registration for any qualified business entity engaged in the practice of public accounting 'except as specifically provided in Section 58-26a-305 or 58-1-307' -- a strict statutory reading gives out-of-state FIRMS no exemption. But the just-amended rule R156-26a-305(3) (retained through the 2026-07-08 amendment) still grants FIRM MOBILITY: an out-of-state firm need not register if its principal place of business is not in Utah, it holds an active unrestricted home-jurisdiction firm license in good standing, and it meets Utah's ownership (58-26a-302(3)(a)(iii)) and peer-review (R156-26a-303a) requirements. Statute and compiled rule state opposite answers, so per the contradiction rule the CONSERVATIVE values are recorded (firm_registration_attest = true, firm_registration_tax = true), with the caveat that the board's own operative rule says qualifying firms are exempt. Watch for conforming legislation or further rulemaking.

events.citation: KRS 325.282 (practice privilege) and KRS 325.301 (firm licensure/exemption), Ky. Rev. Stat. ch. 325; KRS 325.282 as amended by 2026 Ky. Acts ch. 21, sec. 2 (HB 45), effective July 15, 2026
events.detail: THREE distinct flux/conflict elements. (1) RECENT CHANGEOVER, ALREADY OPERATIVE: 2026 HB 45 (2026 Ky. Acts ch. 21, signed by Gov. Beshear 2026-04-03) rewrote the mobility test in KRS 325.282(1) and took effect 2026-07-15 -- only 16 days before this verification. HB 45 struck the old requirement that the CPA hold a license 'from any state that the board has determined to have licensure requirements substantially equivalent to those found in this chapter' (STATE-level substantial equivalency) and replaced it with a test on the INDIVIDUAL: at initial licensure the person must have been required to show evidence of (a) passing a board-approved exam and (b) attaining the education and experience requirements of KRS 325.261(3) and (5). HB 45 also added a new grandfather subsection KRS 325.282(2) preserving privileges for anyone who, as of June 30, 2025, held a CPA license from any state and had KY practice privileges. EFFECTIVE-DATE CHECK PERFORMED: HB 45 contains NO emergency clause and no effective-date section (full GA text is Sections 1-4 only); Kentucky requires an express emergency declaration under Ky. Const. sec. 55 for immediate effect -- there is no supermajority-triggered immediate-effect mechanism, so the vote margins (House 93-0 with 7 not voting of 100 members; Senate 38-0 with 0 not voting of 38 members) do NOT accelerate the date. Default 90-days-after-sine-die (session adjourned 2026-04-15) applies. Confirmed on BOTH legs: LRC compiled statute prints 'Effective: July 15, 2026' and the Board homepage says 'Beginning July 15, 2026'. (Secondary press reporting of 'July 16, 2026' is wrong; do not use.) (2) SOURCE DISAGREEMENT -- STALE BOARD PAGE on equivalence_test: the Board's Reciprocal License page still describes the pre-HB-45 test, requiring that the CPA's home state 'is considered to have licensing requirements substantially equivalent to those of Kentucky' (state-level). That directly contradicts the now-operative individual-criteria test in KRS 325.282(1). The statute controls; equivalence_test is recorded as individual_criteria (which is also the more demanding value for the practitioner, since it requires the individual to have personally met KY's education/experience/exam criteria rather than merely holding a license from an SE state). (3) INTERNAL STATUTORY TENSION on firm_registration_attest: KRS 325.282(6) (renumbered from (5) by HB 45, text carried forward unamended from 2008) says a privileged individual performing an SAS audit, an SSAE examination of prospective financial statements, or a PCAOB engagement for a KY-home-office client 'shall perform the service or services through a firm which has obtained a license issued under KRS 325.301' -- while KRS 325.301(2) (added by 2018 Ky. Acts ch. 24) expressly says an out-of-state firm with no KY office 'shall not be required to obtain a license.' The Board's own published guidance resolves this in favor of firm mobility (no license required), and the chapter's own definition of 'Firm' in KRS 325.220(3) includes an entity that 'is exempt from having to obtain a license pursuant to KRS 325.301.' Recorded as false accordingly, but the 282(6) cross-reference was never conformed and is an unresolved drafting artifact. Separately, compiled 201 KAR 1:050 Sec. 1(2)(d) still requires a transcript verifying 'the 150-hour requirement of KRS 325.261' -- a stale rule now that HB 45 repealed the 150-hour subsection; that stale rule affects LICENSURE, not the mobility test, but signals the Board has not yet run conforming rulemaking. No pending 201 KAR ch. 1 amendment on mobility or firm registration was found in the Administrative Register as of 2026-07-31. UPDATE (verifier): HB 45 sec. 3 ALSO amended KRS 325.280 (reciprocity) effective the same 2026-07-15 date, so the reciprocal-license path this record routes office-opening CPAs into changed simultaneously with the mobility test. The 2025-2026 KRS ch. 325 enactment scan is documented COMPLETE: 2025 Ky. Acts ch. 5 (2025 HB 262) amended KRS 325.380 effective 2025-06-27 (firm-name and deceased/retired-partner rules only, no mobility impact). CONTRADICTION-OF-FORM, not of law: the official catchline of KRS 325.282 still reads "...meeting substantially equivalent licensure requirements" and was not conformed by HB 45 - catchlines are not law under KRS 446.140, so equivalence_test=individual_criteria stands. Correction to the researcher's claim that the Board "has not yet run conforming rulemaking": more precisely, no SUBSTANTIVE conforming amendment is on file, though 201 KAR 1:160 carries a certification effective 2026-03-30.

events.citation: Neb. Rev. Stat. § 1-125.01 (as amended by Laws 2026, LB718, § 5, eff. 2026-07-18); firm permits Neb. Rev. Stat. §§ 1-126, 1-134, 1-135, 1-136; peer review Neb. Rev. Stat. § 1-153 and 288 Neb. Admin. Code ch. 13, § 004.01; practice privilege rule 288 Neb. Admin. Code ch. 7, § 001.02
events.detail: Nebraska joined the 2025-26 wave: LB718 (signed 2026-02-25, no emergency clause, effective 2026-07-18 per the Legislature's compiled-statute effective-date line) rewrote § 1-125.01, moving inbound mobility FROM open CPA=CPA (any active out-of-state CPA license sufficed, 2009 LB31 text now stricken) TO individual-criteria guardrails: the CPA must have passed the Uniform CPA Exam and, at initial licensure, met minimum education/experience requirements defined by the board. Implementing rules (288 NAC ch. 3, 7, 8, 9, 13) were filed/updated 2026-07-25 — 288 NAC 7-001.02A defines the criteria as the three Nebraska pathways (master's+1yr, bachelor's+30hr+1yr, or bachelor's+2yr) and 7-001.02B grandfathers anyone who held privileges as of 2024-12-31. SOURCE DISAGREEMENT on firm registration for non-attest work: the amended statute conditions only ATTEST (for entities with home office in NE) on a firm permit and grants individuals privilege with no notice/fee, but the board's live web guidance (Apply for Permit page: 'Firms must register with the Board if they are practicing public accountancy in the state of Nebraska and/or for a Nebraska client'; firm FAQ: any CPA planning 'public accounting work' in NE 'must license their CPA firm in Nebraska') requires firm registration for ANY Nebraska-client work — the conservative value (firm_registration_tax=true) is recorded per policy. Board mobility page is stale (still points to cpamobility.org and 2010 rule-change documents). UPDATE (verifier): prior-wave context - LB854 (2024, eff. 2025-01-01) lowered exam-sitting eligibility to 120 hours; LB718 completed the licensure-pathway changes.

events.citation: La. R.S. 37:94 (individual practice privileges); La. R.S. 37:77 (firm permits/exceptions); LAC 46:XIX.1105(E) (no-notice/no-fee rule); LAC 46:XIX.1501(B) (firm no-permit conditions)
events.detail: Act 653 of 2026 (HB 548, Rep. Beaullieu), signed 2026-06-02, effective 2026-08-01 (the DAY AFTER this verification date), rewrites R.S. 37:94: section retitled from 'Substantial equivalency' to 'Mobility practice privileges'; the board/designee state-level substantial-equivalence test (NASBA-style) is STRICKEN and replaced with individual criteria — a valid active CPA license in good standing from any state qualifies, with no license, notice, registration, or fee, 'if at the time of initial licensure, the individual was required to show evidence of having passed the uniform CPA examination' and met one of three pathways: (a) baccalaureate + 30 additional semester hours + 1 year experience, (b) post-baccalaureate degree + 1 year experience, or (c) baccalaureate + 2 years experience. New 37:94(A)(2) grandfathers any individual licensed as of 2024-12-31 who had Louisiana practice privileges on that date. The no-notice/no-fee outcome becomes statutory (today it rests on board rule LAC 46:XIX.1105.E.2 adopted under express statutory authorization). Firm statute R.S. 37:77 is NOT amended by Act 653. Board rules LAC 46:XIX.1105(E) and the board's substantially-equivalent-states framework still reflect the pre-Act scheme; conforming rulemaking not yet observed — watch the Louisiana Register. Effective date verified from the official bill-history line 'Effective date: 08/01/2026'; the enrolled act contains no immediate-effect/supermajority clause (votes were 91-0 House, 35-0 Senate, but no such clause exists — Louisiana's default Aug 1 effective date applies). Act read from enrolled PDF rendered visually with strike/underline markup preserved; no statute-vs-act contradiction found. So: equivalence_test is 'nasba_state_level' as of 2026-07-31 and becomes 'individual_criteria' on 2026-08-01. UPDATE (verifier): the 2026-08-01 changeover is ONE DAY after verified_date - re-verify immediately after it takes effect; equivalence_test is expected to flip to individual_criteria per the record's open question.

SB26-076 (signed 2026-05-04, Ch. 81) rewrites CRS 12-100-117(2)(a)(I): from 2026-08-12 an individual out-of-state CPA licensed in good standing with principal place of business elsewhere has ALL the same practice privileges as Colorado certificate holders if, at initial licensure, their licensing state required passing the Uniform CPA Exam and a baccalaureate degree (individual-criteria/near-CPA=CPA test replacing the current NASBA-substantial-equivalency test in Rule 1.14); CPAs holding CO practice privileges as of 2024-12-31 are grandfathered, and the board is statutorily barred from requiring any notice, fee, or other submission. Effective-date verification: the act uses Colorado's standard referendum-petition clause (no supermajority immediate-effect mechanism exists in CO), so the remainder of the act takes effect the day after the 90-day post-adjournment period (GA adjourned 2026-05-13); leg.colorado.gov's official bill history lists '08/12/2026 - Effective date'; only section 1 (12-100-108 licensure pathways: BA+2yr experience / BA+30hr+1yr / post-bacc+1yr) is delayed to 2027-01-01. SB26-076 § 3 also narrows the firm-registration exception cross-reference in 12-100-114(1) from '12-100-117(2)' to '12-100-117(2)(a)(II)' (firm incident-to exception only). Source-disagreement flags: (1) Board Rule 1.14 (3 CCR 705-1, current version eff. 12/15/2024) still states the superseded NASBA-NQAS substantial-equivalency test; conforming board rulemaking is pending (COCPA reports notice-comment-hearing phase next; hearings to post at dpo.colorado.gov/Accountancy_Program_Info, which itself shows stale 2019-2022 content). (2) COCPA (secondary) claims the mobility provisions take effect only when the board adopts implementing rules — the act's own effective-date clause contains no such condition; act text controls.

events.citation: RSMo § 326.283 (individual practice privilege); RSMo § 326.289 (firm permits); 20 CSR 2010-2.022 (Privilege to Practice)
events.detail: TWO issues. (1) ENACTED CHANGE: SB 1233 (2026), signed by Gov. Kehoe July 2026, repeals the substantial-equivalency test in 326.283 and replaces it with INDIVIDUAL CRITERIA: a valid unrestricted license in good standing from any state, provided that at initial licensure the individual passed the Uniform CPA Exam and met one of three education/experience combos (bachelor's + accounting concentration + 2 yrs experience; bachelor's + 30 hrs + 1 yr; post-baccalaureate degree + 1 yr). Grandfather clause preserves privileges for anyone licensed and holding MO practice privileges as of 2024-12-31. No-notice/no-fee language is retained. Also adds a sole-practitioner/single-member-LLC exemption request from the CPA-title firm-permit requirement (non-attest only). The TAT text has NO emergency clause for the accountancy sections (the only contingent-effective-date section, Section B, covers interior-design repeals 324.406/324.424), so ch. 326 changes take effect on Missouri's constitutional default date 2026-08-28; press coverage (Accounting Today, CFO Dive, Inside Public Accounting) uniformly confirms Aug. 28, 2026. On that date equivalence_test flips from nasba_state_level to individual_criteria. (2) SOURCE DISAGREEMENT on firm_registration_attest: compiled statute 326.289.1(2) (as amended 2020, HB 2046) lets a firm with NO office in Missouri perform attest/compilation WITHOUT a permit if it meets ownership, peer-review, practice-privilege-individual, and lawful-in-home-state conditions; but the board's still-compiled rule 20 CSR 2010-2.022(5) (last amended eff. 2012-06-30, authority cites RSMo Supp. 2011) states attest services for a client with a home office in Missouri must be performed 'through a firm holding a current permit to practice in this state,' and the board's Initial Firm Permit application (form 375-0715) still instructs out-of-state firms on obtaining a permit to provide attest/review/compilation services. Per the conservative rule, firm_registration_attest is recorded TRUE (permit required); the statute's no-permit pathway is quoted in the quotes array. No board rulemaking to conform 2.022 to the 2020 statute or to SB 1233 was pending on the DCI proposed-rules page as of 2026-07-31.

events.citation: Ala. Code § 34-1-7 (practice privilege; Act 2009-620 scheme); Ala. Code §§ 34-1-6, 34-1-10, 34-1-11, 34-1-16(12) (firm registration/permits, attest exception); Ala. Admin. Code r. 30-X-3-.04 (Mobility); all as amended by HB59, 2026 Reg. Sess. (Pathways to CPA Act), eff. 2026-10-01
events.detail: HB59 (2026 Reg. Sess., 'Pathways to CPA Act', Rep. Underwood) passed House 20-Jan-26, Senate 22-Jan-26, signed by Gov. Ivey late Jan 2026. Section 3 states a flat effective date: 'This act shall become effective on October 1, 2026.' -- no supermajority/immediate-effect option, so no vote-count analysis needed. It rewrites 34-1-7(a): current law grants practice privilege to any 'person who is licensed as a certified public accountant in another state' (open CPA=CPA, no equivalency test); from 2026-10-01 the individual must ALSO have 'satisfied the educational requirements adopted by rule of the board' -- i.e., Alabama moves to individual-criteria mobility with the education test delegated to board rule. Board rulemaking defining those educational requirements is pending (secondary sources report proposed pathway rules circulating with an Oct 15, 2026 reference); Ala. Admin. Code r. 30-X-3-.04 (last amended eff. 2009-12-23) and the board's mobility web page still state only the pre-HB59 open-license test -- not a present-day contradiction because HB59 is not yet effective, but both will be stale on 2026-10-01 unless updated. Firm-side rules (no registration for firms with no Alabama office, including for attest via the 34-1-16(12) exception for individuals practicing under 34-1-7) are carried forward substantively unchanged by HB59. UPDATE (verifier): ASBPA Notice of Intended Action amending Ch. 30-X-4 filed with LSA 2026-05-08 (comment period closed 2026-07-10); it does NOT amend 30-X-3-.04 and does NOT yet supply the 34-1-7(a) education rule for out-of-state privilege holders. HB59 signing date confirmed: Gov. Ivey announced signing 2026-01-30 ("I have signed HB59, the Pathways to CPA Act"); act number still unlocated - open question retained.

events.detail: HB 4317 (Laws 2026, c. 186) — Oklahoma's UAA 9th-edition rewrite — passed House 83-0 (2026-03-11) and Senate 44-0 (2026-04-29), Governor signed 2026-05-05 (bill history; OSCPA reported May 6). events.detail: Chapter 530 of the Laws of 2025 (S6891B), signed 2025-11-21 and effective 2026-11-21 ('This act shall take effect twelve months after it shall have become a law'), rewrites Educ. Law 7406(2): the current test - licensure by a state the Board of Regents has determined substantially equivalent, or individual qualifications verified by the department - is replaced by individual criteria: valid license in good standing, out-of-state principal place of business, completion of either of the professional education and experience requirements in 7404(1)(2)-(3), and passage of the written examination in 7404(1)(4). events.citation: A.R.S. § 32-725 (limited reciprocity privilege; individuals and out-of-state firms); A.R.S. § 32-731 (CPA firm registration); as amended by Laws 2026, Ch. 17 (SB 1181, Certified Public Accounting Act of 2026) eff. 2027-01-01
events.detail: SB 1181 (Laws 2026, Ch. 17, 'Certified Public Accounting Act of 2026') was signed 2026-04-07 and is enacted but NOT YET EFFECTIVE: the act's own Sec. 18 states 'This act is effective from and after December 31, 2026,' i.e. operative 2027-01-01. This in-act delayed date governs (it is later than the session's general effective date of 2026-09-12 after the 2026-06-13 sine die; no emergency clause, so no supermajority vote-count question arises). The act strikes the current A.R.S. 32-725(B)(4) mobility test (licensing jurisdiction requires 150 semester hours + baccalaureate + passed CPA exam + 1 year verified experience, OR individual meets 32-721(C)) and replaces it with: individual holds an out-of-state CPA license AND either (a) meets the qualifications in 32-721(A) (new pathways: baccalaureate+2yrs experience, baccalaureate+30 extra hours+1yr, or postbaccalaureate+1yr) or 32-4302 (Arizona universal-licensure-recognition statute), or (b) holds a valid active CPA registration/certificate/license from any jurisdiction as of December 31, 2024 (grandfather clause). The no-notice/no-fee provision (32-725(D)) and the out-of-state-firm no-registration provision (32-725(G)) are carried forward unchanged (Ch. 17 also adds out-of-state firms to the 'limited reciprocity privilege' definition). The board's Mobility page currently matches the in-force pre-2027 statute (no stale-page disagreement today), but will need updating at the changeover. UPDATE (verifier): Board Notice of Proposed Expedited Rulemaking (July 2026) implements Laws 2026 Ch. 17 - outlines required accounting/related course hours for certification (which feed the 32-721(A) qualifications the NEW 2027 mobility test cross-references) and reduces reciprocity verifications to one jurisdiction; oral proceeding 2026-08-24, final text pending - recheck after adoption. DIFFLAB WARNING: the board News page headline styles the act '(Effective December 31, 2026)' - that is a paraphrase of the act's 'from and after December 31, 2026' clause; the operative date remains 2027-01-01. Do not let an alert on that phrasing trigger a date change. Board also ran 2025-2026 expedited rule updates on peer review (R4-1-454, May 2025) and CPE (May 2026).

P.A. 104-0228 (HB2459, signed 2025-08-15, eff. 2026-01-01) retitled 225 ILCS 450/5.2 from 'Substantial equivalency' to 'Enhanced mobility' and REPLACED the NASBA NQAS substantial-equivalency test with: (1) issuing state's licensure requirements equivalent to the criteria in Section 14, or (2) individual petition to the Public Accountant Registration and Licensure Committee for an equivalency determination of education, exam, and experience. NOTE: the prior-research claim that IL 'adopted NASBA NQAS state-level equivalency' is BACKWARDS - the enrolled act DELETES the NQAS language (shown stricken in the act). The prior-research claim that the enrolled act and compiled ILCS state DIFFERENT tests could not be reproduced: researcher AND independent adversarial verifier each fetched the enrolled act's raw HTML with strike/underline markup preserved and the compiled ILCS text; both state the SAME new Section-14-equivalence/petition test (compiled source line: 'P.A. 103-309, eff. 1-1-24; 104-228, eff. 1-1-26'). The apparent contradiction arises when the act's STRICKEN NQAS text loses strikethrough formatting during text extraction and reads as live text - both versions are reproduced verbatim in the evidence quotes; human review of the enrolled act PDF should confirm. Still genuinely in flux: (a) Section 14 licensure criteria - the referent of the 5.2(a)(1) equivalence test - gain two new pathways on 2027-01-01 (bachelor's in accounting + 2 yrs experience; master's or bachelor's + 30 accounting hrs + 1 yr), which will shift which states are 'equivalent'; (b) IDFPR's administrative rules (68 Ill. Adm. Code 1420) contain no mobility/practice-privilege section and have not been updated for P.A. 104-0228 (1420.35 Temporary Practice is repealed) - rulemaking is likely; (c) the entire Public Accounting Act is scheduled to be repealed 2029-01-01 (sunset).

events.citation: 22 GCA § 35122 (Substantial Equivalency), Guam Accountancy Act of 2003; firm permits at 22 GCA § 35107; implementing rules at 25 GAR §§ 2103(d), 2106, 2112
events.detail: SOURCE DISAGREEMENT on notice_required and fee_required (no pending legislation). (1) The codified statute, 22 GCA § 35122(a)(1) and (a)(2), states the privilege is automatic and that 'no notice or other submission shall be provided by any such individual.' (2) The Board's own official form, 'Notice of Intent to Practice Public Accountancy in Guam under Substantial Equivalency Provisions of 22 GCA §35122 and 25 GAR §2112' (https://www.guamboa.org/pdf/GU_SE.pdf, HTTP Last-Modified 2019-12-07, i.e. republished THREE YEARS AFTER the no-notice language was enacted), is a notarized filing requiring submission 'within 30 days after accepting an engagement.' (3) The compiled administrative rule 25 GAR § 2103(d)(2) prescribes fees expressly keyed to '22 GCA, § 35122': Initial $225.00, Renewal (annually) $175.00, Reactivation/Reinstatement $275.00, Provisional $175.00. A per-registrant annual renewal fee is only coherent if a registration/notice exists. Both the no-notice statutory language AND the substantial-equivalency fee schedule were enacted by the SAME act, P.L. 33-193 (Dec. 15, 2016), which repealed and reenacted both 22 GCA ch. 35 and 25 GAR ch. 2 — so this is an unresolved internal conflict within enacted Guam law, not a stale rule lagging a new statute. Per the conservative-value rule, notice_required and fee_required are recorded TRUE (the reading requiring more of the practitioner). A secondary, lesser divergence: the Board FAQ Q7 describes an open 'Individual Mobility' privilege for a CPA licensed 'in any other of the 54 U.S. jurisdictions,' which is broader than the statute's NASBA-NQAS substantial-equivalence test; currently harmless because all jurisdictions are NQAS substantially equivalent, but it would diverge if any jurisdiction lost that status. No changeover date applies: Guam has enacted no accountancy amendment since 2016.

events.citation: 4 CMC §§ 3401-3440 (Accountancy Act of 2002, PL 13-52), esp. 4 CMC § 3401 (definitions), § 3422 (issuance/renewal of certificates), § 3423 (firm permits to practice); NMIAC §§ 1-10-801 (interstate practice), 1-10-2301 to 1-10-2310 (substantial equivalency/notification), 1-10-1605 (fees)
events.detail: SOURCE DISAGREEMENT (not a pending legislative change). The CNMI's codified statute contains NO practice-privilege / substantial-equivalency mobility provision at all. The full text of PL 13-52 (Accountancy Act of 2002) was read section-by-section (Sections 1-24): Section 6 (codified 4 CMC § 3422) is titled 'Issuance and Renewal of Certificates' and provides only certificate-by-RECIPROCITY (the applicant applies for and is issued a CNMI certificate); Section 7 (codified 4 CMC § 3423) is firm permits. No section of the Act grants a practice privilege. HOWEVER, the Board's compiled administrative rules repeatedly presuppose a statutory substantial-equivalency standard that does not exist: NMIAC § 1-10-801(a)(2)(i) tells out-of-state individuals they may render services 'pursuant to: (i) Substantial equivalence (see section 6 of the Act [4 CMC § 3422])', NMIAC § 1-10-801(b) refers to 'the substantial equivalency standard set out in the Act, section 6 [4 CMC § 3422]', and NMIAC § 1-10-801(c)(3)-(4) requires notice/consent 'as required for substantially equivalent practitioners under section 6 of the Act [4 CMC § 3422]'. 4 CMC § 3422 as codified by the CNMI Law Revision Commission contains no such standard. The rules appear to have been drafted from the 2004+ UAA model against a statute that was never amended to match. This markup/contradiction was checked: the codified § 3422 (Source: PL 13-52, § 6, modified) and the original enrolled PL 13-52 Section 6 were compared line-by-line and AGREE with each other — so this is not a lost-strikethrough artifact; it is a genuine statute-vs-compiled-rule conflict. Conservative values recorded throughout: privilege treated as existing but conditioned on notice AND fee AND discretionary Board authorization; firm permit required for both attest and tax. No 2025-26 licensure/mobility wave legislation or rulemaking was found for CNMI — the Commonwealth Register is current through Vol. 48 (July 2026) with no Board of Accountancy entries, and the accountancy rules are still the 2007-adopted set as compiled in 2016. UPDATE (verifier - individual_practice_privilege REFUTED true -> set null): NO STATUTE GRANTS A PRACTICE PRIVILEGE. Full-text search of the enrolled PL 13-52 AND the codified 4 CMC 3401/3422/3423 (both downloaded and text-extracted) returns ZERO hits for "substantial equivalen", "practice privilege", or "principal place of business". Codified 4 CMC 3422 is captioned "Issuance and Renewal of Certificates" and 3422(c) provides only that "The Board shall issue a certificate to a holder of a certificate, license, or permit issued by another state upon a showing that:" - that is RECIPROCITY (get a CNMI certificate), not mobility. The sole basis for any privilege is a DISCRETIONARY board rule, NMIAC 1-10-801(c): "the Board MAY authorize the individual to exercise practice privileges in the CNMI provided the individual meets each of the following requirements" - permission on application, not an as-of-right privilege - and it rests on a thin statutory hook. The statute cuts the other way: 4 CMC 3422(a) provides "The holder of a certificate issued under this section may only practice public accountancy in a firm that holds a permit issued under section 3423 of this Act." A permissive true would tell a CPA a privilege exists where the profession's own authority treats CNMI as a non-mobility jurisdiction. null (not_verified) is the honest value: apply to the Board. No CNMI mobility legislation since (Commonwealth Register current through Vol. 48, July 2026, no Board of Accountancy entries; latest public laws PL 24-33/34/35 July 2026, none accountancy).

events.detail: Oregon is mid-wave and has multiple live moving parts. (1) STATUTORY CHANGEOVER ALREADY OPERATIVE: SB 797 (2025) = Or. Laws 2025 ch. 132 rewrote ORS 673.010(20), 673.153, 673.160 and 673.455. EFFECTIVE-DATE CHECK PERFORMED ON THE ACT ITSELF: the enrolled act runs SECTION 1 through SECTION 39 with NO effective-date section, NO operative-date section and NO emergency clause (verified by reading all 26 pages of the enrolled PDF, including pages 25-26; no '2026' string appears anywhere in the act). Oregon Const. Art. IV sec. 28 sets only a 90-day floor, but the operative default is statutory: ORS 171.022 -- 'an Act of the Legislative Assembly takes effect on January 1 of the year after passage.' 2025 regular session adjourned sine die 2025-06-27. Legislative Counsel's own ORS annotation confirms the date by printing the editorial gloss 'the effective date of this 2025 Act [January 1, 2026]' in the Note following ORS 673.410. Therefore rule_changes_on = 2026-01-01. No supermajority/immediate-effect analysis was needed because the act contains no such option. (2) BOARD RULE CHANGEOVER: BOA 1-2026, amend filed 01/29/2026, effective 02/01/2026, conformed OAR ch. 801 to SB 797. Materially, it DELETED the old mobility subsection (1) of OAR 801-010-0080 and retitled that rule 'Applications by Reciprocity' -- confirmed by the OSCPA comment published on the board's own past-rulemaking page ('The proposed draft removes subsection (1) but retains subsection (4) (renumbered as subsection (2))... the omission of subsection (1) eliminates explicit OAR language on mobility'). Net effect: individual mobility now rests on ORS 673.153 alone, with no implementing OAR. (3) OPEN RULEMAKING RIGHT NOW: the board's rulemaking page states rulemaking began June 4 with rule exposure 2026-07-01 and a public comment period running 2026-07-01 through 9:00 a.m. 2026-09-24. The exposed rule list is not published on that page, so it is unknown whether mobility/firm-registration rules are in scope. The same page also flags board/LRC policy work on private-equity ownership of CPA firms, which would touch ORS 673.160 firm requirements. (4) SOURCE DISAGREEMENT ON FIRM-REGISTRATION SCOPE: OAR 801-010-0345(3) requires out-of-state firms serving Oregon clients to register if they perform 'Attestation engagements' or PCAOB engagements. 'Attestation services' under ORS 673.010(1) and the board's own OAR 801-005-0010 definition includes SSARS reviews (para. (b)) and other SSAE examination/review/agreed-upon-procedures work (para. (d)). But ORS 673.160(1)(c) triggers registration ONLY for 673.010(1)(a) SAS audits, (c) SSAE examinations of prospective financial information, and (e) PCAOB engagements, and ORS 673.160(3)(a) expressly EXEMPTS out-of-state firms doing 673.010(1)(b)/(d) work and compilations. The board's own peer-review web page follows the narrower statutory reading ('Out-of-state firms performing compilation and/or review services for Oregon clients are not required to register with the Board'). The compiled rule is therefore BROADER than the statute. Because both sources answer firm_registration_attest 'true', the conservative value is recorded either way; the disagreement affects only which engagement types trigger it, and the conservative (rule-based, broader) reading is described in notes. (5) STALE BOARD WEB GUIDANCE: the board's licensee-FAQ page and its License Application Requirements page still cite 'substantial equivalency as defined in ORS 673.010(21)' -- that is the PRE-2026 cross-reference that SB 797 sec. 12 struck out of ORS 673.153(1) and renumbered; the current definition sits at ORS 673.010(20) with new three-pathway criteria. OAR 801-010-0080's 'Statutes/Other Implemented' line still lists ORS 673.040, which SB 797 sec. 37 REPEALED. These are stale-citation defects, not substantive conflicts, but they show board guidance trailing the statute.
